    - Kestra. I string the rope bridges across the clefts of the cliff, from the low spans over the quay to the highest one near the top. I can cross any of them blindfold. I have, for bets.
    - Gorm took me on as a rope-carrier at fourteen, mostly to stop me climbing things. It did not work.
    - My mother, Shona, made nets in the coves. She taught me every knot she knew before I could write my name. She died of a fever when I was fifteen, and I just stayed up on the bridges.
    - Old Agna calls my knots Shona's knots, near enough. Near enough is the nicest thing Agna says about anyone. There. Now you know where the knots come from.
    - Every morning I walk every bridge end to end, hands on the ropes, listening to the planks. What is worn I replace before it frays. What is frayed I replace before anyone notices.
    - Help me check every lashing on one of them and I will teach you **Rope Slide**: the quick way down a rope or ladder, and safely off its end.
    - Every morning, every bridge, end to end. Hands on the ropes, ears on the planks. You have checked my lashings yourself now, so you know.
    - Use your **Rope Slide** on the Saltface. That cliff is all ropes and ledges. And look where you are going, not where you might land.
    - The highest bridge. Something is chewing the ropes. Not frayed, not cut. Chewed, from below, on the seaward side, strand by strand, where nothing should be able to reach.
    - I splice them and it happens again. I have never once seen what does it. Tarran is making me a lantern to light the face under the bridge. I am waiting for it. Patiently. Do not laugh.
    - I know what is down there now. What frightens me is someone who does not know the ropes stepping onto that bridge on the night it gives. So it never gives. That is the whole job.
    - Feet first, eyes forward.
